planes not allowed to fly over the island 
require a special licence to fly a drone on the island
how the property market operates

No mention of the other financial contribution to the island's economy. 
Because of the very low tax levels on Sark, companies would register their companies there. Ordinary residents became directors of multiple companies in return for their homes becoming the official registered office. 
This was known as "The Sark Lark"! 
I don't know if this still happens but it certainly used to.

replies.author: @abundantplanet
replies.text: There is no mains water supply - each household is responsible for obtaining their own water either through a private borehole, a water well or water catchment. Neither do they have a mains sewage  system. Again each household is responsible for handling their own foul water using private pits and septic tanks which are emptied by the island administration. Sark has one electricity company that supplies residential and commercial properties. Warmth to homes is provided by electric, bottled gas, oil or / and wood burners - all of which makes it expensive to run a property

🇬🇧 According to Wikipedia.

Sark - is an island in the southwestern English Channel, off the coast of Normandy, and part of the archipelago of the Channel Islands. It is part of the Bailiwick of Guernsey, a self-governing British Crown Dependency, with its own set of laws based on Norman law, and its own parliament. It was a royal fiefdom until 2008, when the Constitution of Sark went into effect.

Note: a self-governing British Crown Dependency.
